identity.real_world_identity_notes: The officially licensed Brazilian Sprint Race one-make car announced for AMS2 in 2019: a centrally seated, rear-wheel-drive 260 hp V6 car with a six-speed sequential transmission. The official announcement does not say whether that transmission is lever- or paddle-actuated; the current AMS2 cockpit observation establishes paddles for this simulator entry.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behavior was observed in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled.
The real-car source establishes only a six-speed sequential transmission; paddle actuation, cut, blip and wheel details come from the current AMS2 drive.
The wheel has molded side grips and a central control face, so it is classified gt-formula even though it has neither an integrated display nor shift lights.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.sprint-race.20260822t040810093z-2415554e by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: The official Reiza announcement establishes the licensed 2019 car and six-speed sequential transmission, while the guided drive establishes its AMS2 paddle actuation and shift behavior.

claims.basis: Reiza's official 2019 development update names and describes the licensed Sprint Race car, corroborated by the series' own history.

Reiza specifies a six-speed sequential transmission. The current guided cockpit drive establishes sequential paddles, automatic cut, automatic blip and the wheel layout in AMS2; the official source is silent on those details.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Six-speed paddle car with a GT/formula-style rim. Use the clutch to launch, then stay flat for upshifts; AMS2 cuts and blips automatically.
